hero_title: Get Notified When Terminal and AI Tasks Finish.
hero_desc: Start your work and step away from the screen. Mample notifies your phone when your builds, terminal commands and AI tasks finish. No subscriptions, no monthly notification quota. 100% free.
about_desc: Mample connects your phone to your terminal and AI coding workflow. Install the CLI, pair with QR or the mobile app’s Secret Key, and send a message when a task finishes. No email/password registration is needed. Browser integration has a separate development scope.
sec_1_title: Are My Codes and Data Safe?
sec_1_desc: The CLI sends the notification message you provide through Firebase; it does not automatically collect source code or terminal output. The notification service processes the content of your message.
sec_2_desc: Messages are held temporarily in the delivery queue and removed after processing. The latest notification history is stored locally on your phone.
sec_3_title: Do I Need Email or Password Registration?
sec_3_desc_1: No email or password registration is needed; Firebase creates an anonymous session for your device. Your terminal pairs with a unique

privacy_1_p1: Mample uses anonymous Firebase authentication; it does not require email/password registration. The following data is processed to deliver notifications:
privacy_1_li1: Device and connection records: Firebase stores the anonymous user ID, FCM delivery token, CLI Secret Key hash, random terminal connection identifier, device/terminal name, connected devices, notification preferences and anti-abuse rate-limit records.
privacy_1_li2: CLI messages: the CLI sends the message you provide. It does not automatically collect your source code or terminal output.
privacy_1_li3: Delivery and history: notification content is held temporarily in a Firebase delivery queue and removed after processing. The mobile app stores the most recent 50 notifications locally.
privacy_2_desc: Mample does not offer premium purchases or subscriptions and does not use RevenueCat. No payment information is collected by the app.
privacy_3_desc: The CLI Secret Key is stored in secure storage on the phone and in the local CLI configuration file on your paired computer with user-specific access permissions. The key is transmitted over HTTPS for authentication; the Firebase user record stores its SHA-256 hash. Do not share your key or CLI configuration file. New keys use secure random values; rotating the key invalidates the previous key for CLI requests.
privacy_4_desc: Google Firebase processes authentication, device/connection records and notification delivery data. Firebase SDKs may also process IP addresses, installation identifiers and technical request information to operate the service and prevent abuse. The website is hosted on Vercel. These providers process data under their own policies.
privacy_5_desc: The website uses Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights to measure visits and performance. Hosting providers may process technical request metadata. Mample does not display advertising on the website.
privacy_6_desc: Reset Data clears local notification history, removes connected-device records and rotates the CLI key. It does not delete the anonymous Firebase user record. To request deletion of remaining server data, email odun.coop@gmail.com with the subject “Mample data deletion request”. Do not send your secret key. Additional information may be needed to verify that the relevant record belongs to you.
privacy_7_desc: If you have any questions about our privacy policy, you can contact us at: odun.coop@gmail.com
terms_1_desc: Mample is a notification tool created for developers to track long-running processes. Using the system to send spam notifications, intentionally exceed API limits, or engage in malicious activities is prohibited.
terms_2_desc: Mample provides the mobile app and CLI without premium subscriptions or a monthly notification quota.
terms_2_li1: Short-term request limits may temporarily reject excessive notification traffic to protect the service.
terms_2_li2: Abusive traffic may be restricted or disabled. Service availability depends on network access, infrastructure capacity and operating costs.
terms_3_title: 3. Service Interruption and Disclaimer of Warranty
terms_3_desc: Mample does its best to deliver notifications to your device as quickly as possible but cannot be held responsible for potential notification delays caused by network latency, mobile OS background restrictions, or Firebase outages.
guide_page_desc: Set up Mample for terminal commands and AI coding assistants. Browser extension instructions are on the separate Extension page.
guide_sec0_desc: Mample is designed with a privacy-first approach and a lightweight architecture. Here are the technical details of how the system works behind the scenes:
guide_sec0_li1_desc: The browser extension never reads network traffic or your personal data. It solely relies on a DOM Observer mechanism to detect the visibility of the specific HTML element you selected. When the element is removed from the DOM, it fires a trigger.
guide_sec0_li2_desc:
The CLI runs when invoked; it does not automatically watch terminal tasks in the background. It sends your message to Firebase over HTTPS.

QR and manual Secret Key entry create the same terminal connection. Pairing the same computer with a different mobile installation changes the destination for future messages. Multiple computers can pair with the same phone’s key.

The QR invitation is short-lived; the terminal connection has no automatic expiry. Remove it in the app or with mample disconnect. Rotating the Secret Key on your phone invalidates the old key; pair your terminals again.
guide_sec0_li3_desc: Mample uses an AI assistant’s ability to run terminal commands. Ask it to run the global mample command after completing a task. Mample does not detect task completion itself; terminal access and command permissions depend on the assistant.
guide_sec0_li4_desc: Firebase Cloud Messaging delivers notifications to your phone. Firebase stores an anonymous user ID, an FCM token, a hash of the CLI Secret Key, connected devices and notification preferences. Notification messages are held temporarily in a delivery queue and removed after processing. The last 50 notification history entries are kept on the phone.
guide_sec0_li5_desc: Mample has no premium tier, subscription or monthly notification quota. Short-term rate limits protect the service from spam. Changing phones requires pairing the new mobile installation with your terminal again.
guide_sec1_desc: Mample sends messages to your phone from terminal commands and AI assistants with terminal access. Browser integration is documented separately as a development scope on the Extension page.
guide_sec1_subdesc: Mample can generally be used in two different ways:
guide_sec1_box1_desc: It works by detecting the disappearance of an element during downloads you make via the browser or on web pages where you are waiting for a process.
guide_sec1_box2_desc: Added to the end of long-running commands or compilations running in your computer's terminal, it alerts you when the process is complete.
guide_sec2_sub0_desc: Find the existing Chrome extension link in the browser extensions section above. This guide documents the extension workflow; check the homepage for mobile app availability.
guide_sec2_sub1_desc:
You can instantly connect your device by scanning the QR Code in your browser extension with the Mample app on your mobile device, or by entering your Secret Key into the relevant field in the extension. You can view the connection in the "Connected Devices" section of your mobile app.

For your security, all extension connections are automatically disconnected after 23 hours. You can also manually disconnect instantly by clicking the "Disconnect" icon (broken chain) on your phone or from your extension.
guide_sec2_sub2_title: Receiving Notifications by Selecting a Key
guide_sec2_sub2_desc:
You can teach Mample which button to track by typing /mample on any website or clicking the Select Key button in the extension. When you do this, a key selection interface will appear on the screen. The button you select should be a static, non-animated element that appears when the process starts and disappears when it ends. For example, a 'Stop generating' or 'Cancel' button. Once trained, Mample will send you a notification when the selected button disappears. Your selected button is saved, and you won't need to select it again.

Once your key is set, you have two ways to get notified:

1. Using a Command: Simply type /mample at the end of your prompt. Mample will track that specific process and notify you once.

2. Using the Extension: For websites where you cannot type a prompt, or for a fully automated experience, you can check the Get Notifications from Selected Key option in the extension. This way, you will automatically receive a notification every time your trained button disappears.

You can manage and delete your trained sites using the ☰ menu in the extension.

IMPORTANT NOTE: We strongly recommend keeping the tab and window active while waiting for a process. Most modern websites pause their HTML rendering to save resources when placed in the background. Because the website does not update its interface while hidden, Mample cannot detect that the process has finished until you switch back to the tab.
guide_sec2_sub5_desc: By enabling the Get Notifications for Downloads option in the extension, you can receive a notification when files larger than your specified MB limit finish downloading.

guide_sec4_sub1_title: Setup and Connection in Code Editors (IDE)
guide_sec4_sub1_desc: First pair your terminal with the mobile app using the CLI setup steps. An AI coding assistant that can execute terminal commands can then call Mample when its task finishes.
guide_sec4_sub2_desc: Add “When the task is complete, run mample "Task completed" in the terminal.” to your instructions. The assistant needs terminal access and permission to execute the command. Mample does not monitor task status itself; the notification is sent when the assistant runs the command.
guide_sec4_sub3_desc: Your assistant may request permission before running mample. Permission prompts and persistent approvals vary by assistant, editor and execution environment.
guide_sec4_sub3_desc2: Review the command and message before approving. If supported, you can grant persistent permission specifically for mample. A new environment, different command or security policy may require another approval; Mample does not change these policies.
guide_sec4_sub4_desc: Add this instruction to a project rule file supported by your assistant: “When the task is complete, send a brief notification using the global mample command within existing terminal permissions. Do not include secrets in the message.” Example files: CLAUDE.md and setup.md. These files do not grant execution permissions or remove security prompts.
guide_faq_q1: Does Mample read my code or terminal output?
guide_faq_a1: The CLI sends the notification message you provide. It does not upload your project or collect terminal output automatically. Avoid including information in a message that you do not want transmitted through Firebase.
guide_faq_q2: How is data privacy technically ensured? Where is my data stored and what cloud infrastructure do you use?
guide_faq_a2: Mample uses Firebase anonymous authentication instead of email/password registration. Firebase holds the device delivery token, a hash of your CLI key, connection details, preferences and rate-limit counters. Messages are temporarily queued for delivery. Notification history is stored locally on your phone. Operational logs may also be processed by the hosting providers.
guide_faq_q3: What happens when I change my phone?
guide_faq_a3: Install Mample on the new phone and pair your terminal using that installation's Secret Key. There is no premium entitlement or purchase to transfer.
guide_faq_q4: Is there a limit to how many terminal alerts I can send?
guide_faq_a4: There is no monthly notification quota. To prevent spam, the current backend allows up to 5 requests per connection or CLI key and 20 requests per user across all connections in a rolling 60-second window. A rejected request returns a retry time; wait before trying again.
guide_faq_a5: Browser integration is planned. Find the existing extension and its documentation on the Extension page. Mample currently focuses on the mobile app and CLI.
guide_faq_q6: Which AI assistants does it work with? Is it only for IDEs?
guide_faq_a6: Use Mample with AI assistants that can execute terminal commands and have the required permissions. No dedicated IDE plugin is needed; the assistant runs the global mample command after the task. Chat interfaces without terminal access cannot send notifications directly through this workflow.
guide_faq_q7: Why should I choose Mample over other notification apps or bot software?
guide_faq_a7: Mample combines a mobile app and a lightweight terminal command. Once paired, you can send a message with mample or add it after a build. AI assistants with terminal access can use the same command. Mample is completely free, without a monthly notification quota.

guide_troubleshooting_desc: Check the phone and computer internet connections, the Android notification permission for Mample and the Connected Devices entry in the app. Send a direct test message before adding Mample to a long command. Battery saving and background restrictions can delay delivery.
guide_rate_limit_desc: If you send too frequently, the CLI reports a wait time. Wait before trying again. There is no monthly quota; short-term limits prevent spam.
